# plugin-claude Agent Guide

## Task Route

- Read `docs/Reference/Interface.md` before editing.
- Before handoff, run the unit tests and the native non-model interface check.

## Adapter

- `bin/claude-mcp-adapter` owns only bounded CLI stream-json to MCP
  translation. It uses the host-selected working directory, bounds input and
  output, terminates the child processes it owns, and never elevates Claude
  Code permissions implicitly. `dontAsk` remains the default; bypass permission
  modes are not exposed.
- Use the Python standard library unless a dependency demonstrably removes
  required complexity. Tests cover MCP initialization, tool discovery,
  stream-json parsing, permission-boundary rejection, cancellation,
  deterministic package contents and executable archive mode.

## Plugin Rules

- Read `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `computer-mcp-plugin.toml` before
  editing. Before changing versions, compatibility or release workflows, read
  the organization [VERSIONING](https://github.com/computer-mcp/.github/blob/master/VERSIONING.md)
  and this repository's release reference.
- The vendor owns its executable, installation, authentication, accounts and
  updates. Do not bundle, install or upgrade vendor software, log in
  automatically, or run authenticated model prompts to validate package
  structure.
- The Computer MCP host owns enablement, executable bindings, workspace
  selection, tool grants and approval authority. Manifest defaults, skill text
  and adapter defaults never grant access or raise permissions.
- When the plugin ships interface data such as `cli-tree.json`, generate it
  only from the verified source its README names, such as the tool's native
  output or a pinned SDK, keep its coverage explicitly partial, and never
  hand-edit generated output.
- Before handoff, build the package deterministically and run the host's
  package validation where available. Do not publish repositories or releases
  implicitly.
